We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have identified possible building blocks: a para-methyl phenyl sulfonyl attached to an aniline (sulfonamide). The target has two aromatic rings: a tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) attached via sulfonamide to another phenyl bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamoyl amide) attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). Actually the second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) is attached to sulfonyl, and has a para-substituted trans-α,β-unsaturated amide: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (aniline). So overall: tolyl-sulfonyl-para-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2.

We need retrosynthesis steps: maybe disconnection at sulfonamide bond (S-N) and at amide bond (C=O-N). Also maybe at the C=C double bond (C-C bond formation via Heck or Wittig). But we have only 3 steps.

Potential route:

Step 1: Form sulfonamide between tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and the aniline of the second phenyl (which is para-aminophenyl). Actually the sulfonamide attaches to the aniline of the second phenyl (the phenyl bearing the cinnamoyl amide). So we can start from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) that already has the cinnamoyl amide attached? Wait the amide attaches to the same phenyl at para position relative to sulfonamide? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl via N (sulfonamide). The phenyl ring has the cinnamoyl amide at para position relative to sulfonamide? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl via N (NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl). The phenyl has substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N at para position (maybe). So we need to have that phenyl with both substituents.

We could construct the phenyl core with the cinnamoyl amide first, then sulfonylate.

Option: Start from 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Actually we need trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to phenyl via C=C double bond. Could be formed via Knoevenagel condensation between 4-aminobenzaldehyde and N-phenylglycine? But we need amide attached to phenyl (anilide). Another approach: start from trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) then convert to acid chloride then amidate with 4-aminophenyl (aniline). That gives 4-(cinnamoylamido)phenyl. Then sulfonylate the aniline (the same aniline? Wait the aniline is the same as the amide nitrogen? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is an aniline (para-aminophenyl). The amide is C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl ring that has an NH2 at para? Actually the SMILES: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. That is an amide attached to an aniline (aniline with NH2). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which has an NH2 at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an NH2 at position 1 and another NH2? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an NH attached to the aromatic carbon (the amide nitrogen) and also an NH2 substituent at the other end of the ring (para?). Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" indicates an aniline where the ring has an NH attached at position 1 (the amide N) and an NH2 at position? The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That is an aniline with two amino groups: one attached to the ring (as substituent) and one as part of the amide? The first N is the amide nitrogen attached to the carbonyl; then "c3ccccc3N" indicates the phenyl ring with an NH2 substituent at the para position? Actually the SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" means the amide nitrogen attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) and the ring also has an NH2 at the other end (position 1?). This is ambiguous.

But likely the target is a bis-aniline sulfonamide with a cinnamoyl amide linking to an aniline.

Simplify: we can propose a route:

Step A (final): Sulfonylation of 4-aminophenyl-cinnamoyl-aniline (i.e., 4-[(E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamido]aniline) with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride to give target.

Step B: Formation of the amide: coupling of trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) with 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine). Actually we need an amide where the carbonyl attached to the trans-alkene and to the aniline (p-aminophenyl). So we can take trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) and convert to acid chloride (via SOCl2) then react with p-phenylenediamine (commercial) to give the amide where the carbonyl attaches to one amine, leaving the other amine free for later sulfonylation. That yields 4-(cinnamoylamido)aniline.

Step C: Starting materials: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and the product from step B.

Thus total steps: 2 steps (amide formation, sulfonylation). However we need to consider that the amide formation may be considered a step (activation + coupling). Could be done in one step using coupling reagents (e.g., EDC). So overall 2 steps.

We need to ensure all leaves are commercially available: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, trans-cinnamic acid, p-phenylenediamine (or 4-aminophenylamine). All are likely buyable.

We need to verify each step with templates.

We need to retrieve template IDs for sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine) and amide formation (acid chloride + amine). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_formed = ["sulfonamides"] for sulfonylation, and functional_groups_formed = ["amides"] for amide formation.

Let's search for amide formation using acid chloride + amine. Use functional_groups_formed ["amide"].
